financials_interim.company_name: Lanka Credit and Business Finance PLC
financials_interim.notes: LCBF = Lanka Credit and Business Finance PLC, a CBSL-licensed finance company (NBFI), NOT a fund or SGD-denominated instrument -- despite 'SGD' appearing in the source filename, the cover page and every statement in the filing are denominated in ordinary Sri Lankan Rupees (Rs.); currency is LKR as normal and no SGD adjustment was needed (the filename appears to be a mislabeled/misnamed upload). FYE 31 March; this is Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026). NBFI field mapping per project convention: revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (Rs.340,481,021, i.e. net interest income + net fee income + other operating income, AFTER interest expense); operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services' (Rs.137,483,766), the company's own subtotal before the separate 'Taxes on Financial Services' (SSCL/VAT-FS) line of Rs.38,850,000; tax_expense = Income Tax expense ONLY (Rs.26,000,000) -- Taxes on Financial Services is already netted between operating_profit and profit_before_tax, confirmed by the tie-out 137,483,766 - 38,850,000 = 98,633,766 = profit_before_tax, and 98,633,766 - 26,000,000 = 72,633,766 = profit_after_tax exactly (no column-swap issues found). cost_of_sales/gross_profit/current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables/finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK per NBFI convention -- no current/non-current split is presented and the loan book is not a trade receivable. Borrowings kept conservative: short_term_borrowings = 'Due to Banks' (Rs.2,133,779,168, revolving/short-term facilities); long_term_borrowings = 'Debt Securities' (Rs.200,042,833, the 5-year Tier-2 subordinated bonds maturing Oct-2030 per Note 12). 'Due to Customers' (Rs.6,060,135,728, deposits) is explicitly EXCLUDED from borrowings, per instructions -- customer deposits are not debt for this purpose. unit_scale='1' since the filing reports whole Rupees, not '000. Verified: EPS Rs.0.09 = Rs.72,633,766 / 790,168,780 shares (matches filing, rounds to 0.09). Balance-sheet identity ties: Total Assets Rs.12,396,271,646 = Total Liabilities Rs.8,944,911,718 + Total Equity Rs.3,451,359,928.

interim_updates.company_name: Lanka Credit and Business Finance PLC
interim_updates.note_text: Lanka Credit and Business Finance PLC's Q1 FY2026/27 Total Operating Income grew 21.0% YoY to Rs.340.48Mn, as Interest Income rose 36.5% to Rs.548.03Mn on strong loan-book growth (Loans segment income +39.1% YoY to Rs.453.32Mn), though Interest Expenses rose faster at 62.2% to Rs.226.17Mn as the book was funded with costlier debt -- Net Interest Income therefore grew a slower 22.8% to Rs.321.86Mn. Impairment charges surged 80.0% YoY to Rs.35.27Mn (from Rs.19.59Mn), even as asset quality itself improved (Net Non-Performing Loans ratio 6.02% vs 7.89% a year earlier) -- the higher charge reflects book growth and IFRS 9 provisioning on the larger loan portfolio rather than deteriorating quality. Personnel costs rose 30.4% to Rs.90.98Mn. Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services still grew a healthy 12.0% to Rs.137.48Mn, but the total tax burden (Taxes on Financial Services + Income Tax) rose from Rs.45.27Mn to Rs.64.85Mn (+43.3%) -- driven specifically by Income Tax expense DOUBLING from Rs.13.0Mn to Rs.26.0Mn (+100%) while Taxes on Financial Services rose a further 20.4% to Rs.38.85Mn. As a result, Profit for the Period fell 6.3% YoY to Rs.72.63Mn (EPS Rs.0.09 vs Rs.0.10) despite PBT growing 9.0% to Rs.98.63Mn.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for LCBF -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance-sheet YoY (Total Assets/Total Liabilities) uses the 30 June 2025 figures disclosed in the filing's own Segmental Analysis note (Total Assets Rs.9,270.40Mn, Total Liabilities Rs.6,069.47Mn), since the primary Statement of Financial Position only provides a 31 March 2026 comparative column, not 30 June 2025; total equity for the prior period was not separately disclosed for that date and was not stored (only derivable as a residual, Rs.3,200.92Mn, from the segmental note's asset/liability totals).
interim_updates.takeaway: Profit for the Period fell 6.3% YoY (Rs.77.52Mn -> Rs.72.63Mn) despite Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services growing a healthy 12.0% (Rs.122.79Mn -> Rs.137.48Mn) -- the swing is entirely a tax story, not a core-earnings story. Income tax expense doubled (Rs.13.0Mn -> Rs.26.0Mn, +100%) while Taxes on Financial Services also rose 20.4%, together consuming all of the operating profit growth and more. Underlying operating momentum (interest income +36.5%, Loans segment income +39.1%) is genuinely strong, and the Net NPL ratio actually improved (7.89% -> 6.02%); the bottom-line decline reflects a higher effective tax rate this quarter, not weaker core performance.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services (Rs.)

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income grew 21.0% YoY to Rs.340.48Mn as Interest Income rose 36.5% to Rs.548.03Mn, though Interest Expenses rose faster at 62.2% to Rs.226.17Mn.
Impairment charges surged 80.0% YoY to Rs.35.27Mn (from Rs.19.59Mn), a drag on Net Operating Income (+16.6% to Rs.305.21Mn, slower than the 21% income growth).

Operating Profit before Tax on Financial Services grew 12.0% to Rs.137.48Mn, but combined tax charges (Financial Services tax + Income Tax) rose 43.3% to Rs.64.85Mn, driving Profit for the Period down 6.3% to Rs.72.63Mn.
Loans segment income (the dominant book) grew 39.1% YoY to Rs.453.32Mn; Net Non-Performing Loans ratio improved to 6.02% from 7.89% a year earlier even as impairment charges rose.

Net cash used in operating activities was Rs.(217.60)Mn (vs Rs.+63.83Mn a year ago), driven by a Rs.229.52Mn net outflow in Due to Customers (deposit withdrawals) alongside continued loan book growth.
key_drivers: Doubling of Income Tax expense (Rs.13.0Mn -> Rs.26.0Mn, +100%) is the single specific driver that turned solid operating growth into a bottom-line profit decline.
Impairment charge growth (+80.0% to Rs.35.27Mn) on the Loans segment is a specific, growing cost pressure, even though the Net NPL ratio itself improved (7.89% -> 6.02%).
Higher-cost funding (Interest Expenses +62.2%) compressed net interest margin despite strong topline loan growth, specifically as Due to Banks/deposit funding mix shifted.
